audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Levels 3, 4-5 and First item to K'Sante and Level 2 to Skill, while whys[2] ('you kite with the Boomerang slow... while K'Sante must walk through it in melee'), whys[3] ('you out-trade him outright') and whys[5] ('your Mini-form poke keeps you ahead') all say the opposite. Level 6 was given to Gnar at 7/10 while whys[4] literally opens 'Genuinely even at 6'.
audit.why: The packet chart reads Gnar/Gnar/Gnar/Gnar/Skill/Gnar/K'Sante and the win rate is 52.93% over 1213 games — a Gnar-favoured lane that loses only to scaling. The chart was inverted against its own prose at five of seven rows.
audit.corrected: Levels 2, 3, 4-5 and First item flipped to Gnar with ratings raised; Level 6 flipped to Skill at 5/10 to match whys[4]; 2+ items left with K'Sante, which is the one row that was already right.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page repeatedly says to trade 'when his Q is down' and to track All Out, with no cooldown for either.
audit.why: Ntofo Strikes is a flat 3.5 seconds — it is never down, so waiting it out is not a plan; what you actually dodge is the second stack's shockwave. Footwork is 10/9.5/9/8.5/8, which is the shield window that decides whether a Wallop commit lands. All Out is 120/100/80.
audit.corrected: 3.5s Q and the two-stack mechanic written into early; Footwork's 8-10s shield window written into mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: Five fields call Ntofo Strikes a knockup ('his Q knockup', 'Dodge his Q knockups', 'Land Q's knockup', 'before K'Sante has Q to knock you up', 'Get walled by his Q'). Two fields say Path Maker blocks the Boomerang projectile. Path Maker's true damage, Footwork's shield and All Out's healing were all absent.
audit.why: Riot's Ntofo Strikes text gives damage and a slow in a line, and at 2 stacks a shockwave that PULLS enemies in — there is no knockup anywhere in it. The knock-back and stun live on Path Maker (W). Path Maker's text says K'Sante takes reduced damage while charging; it does not block or destroy projectiles, so 'W blocks your Boomerang' overstates it into a rule the reader will play around wrongly. Path Maker also deals true damage, so armour is the wrong answer to it; Footwork shields on an 8-10s cooldown and eats the burst half of a Wallop commit; and All Out grants increased healing, which is what justifies the Executioner's the item block already recommends.
audit.corrected: Knockup replaced with the two-stack pull in whys[1], spikes[0].text, early and wants.foe[1]; the projectile-block claim softened to damage reduction in early, wants.you[2] and wants.foe[0]; true damage and the Footwork shield added to mid; All Out's healing added to late.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are yours. In Mini form your ranged autos plus a single Boomerang slow win the first trade outright, and K'Sante has to walk into melee with no ranged answer to the harass. Level 2 Hyper is the spike: the third consecutive hit on him procs bonus magic damage and a move-speed burst, which combined with the Boomerang slow lands a chunky free trade and lets you shove. Watch his W — it blocks your Boomerang and dashes him onto you, so throw Q only when his W is already spent, not when he's holding it up. Don't trade into his Q knockup while your Rage bar is empty and you're stuck in fragile Mini.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are yours. In Mini form your ranged autos plus a single Boomerang slow win the first trade outright, and K'Sante has to walk into melee with no ranged answer to the harass. Level 2 Hyper is the spike: the third consecutive hit on him procs bonus magic damage and a move-speed burst, which with the Boomerang slow lands a chunky free trade and lets you shove. Ntofo Strikes is a flat 3.5s, so you never wait it out — what you dodge is the second stack, whose shockwave pulls you in. Path Maker takes reduced damage while it charges and then dashes onto you with a knock-back stun, so throw Q after it, never into it.

edits.before: This is where you press your lead. When Rage fills you transform to Mega and get a Wallop stun in a line into a follow-up, and that punishes him hard for stepping up to last-hit a wave on your side. Keep the wave central or slightly toward you so he must walk into your range to farm. The danger is form timing — if you're stuck in Mini with Rage on cooldown when he hits 6, his All Out can dash in, strip his own armor and MR for the burst, and isolate you with no escape. Only commit the all-in when you're in Mega with Wallop or the ult live, or when his R is down.
edits.after: This is where you press your lead. When Rage fills you transform to Mega and get a Wallop stun in a line into a follow-up, and that punishes him for stepping up to last-hit on your side. Keep the wave central or slightly toward you so he must walk into range to farm. Footwork shields him every 8-10s, so bait it before you spend the Wallop, and Path Maker's damage is true — armour reads that trade wrong. The danger is form timing: caught in Mini with Rage down at his 6, All Out dashes in, strips his own armour and MR for the burst, and isolates you. Commit only in Mega, or while his R is down.

edits.before: Close it before two items. You out-poke and out-trade K'Sante all through laning, but he's a hard scaler — once he has his tank-fighter core he eats your Mega burst, survives the Wallop-into-ult, and reclaims the straight duel with his passive percent-HP damage and the All Out resist-strip all-in. Your value shifts to teamfights, where the Mega ult is still elite engage and peel — flinging his team into a wall for the extended stun. Don't try to solo him in the sidelane late; build your kiting lead early so his scaling never gets to matter.

All Out also grants him increased healing, so Executioner's needs to be down before you contest an extended fight. notes: The 'Q knockup' error also lives in three full-layer strings I could not edit: dosFull[2].t 'Dodge his Q knockups' (20 chars) and dontsFull[0].t 'Get walled by his Q' (19 chars) are both under the applier's 25-character skip threshold, and report[11].t repeats 'Get walled by his Q' inside a longer string. Ntofo Strikes has no knockup and no wall interaction — the pull is a shockwave at 2 stacks, and the only wall effect in the matchup is K'Sante's own R launching a target through terrain. Those three want a manual pass. Note also that the anti-heal advice in report[8].t and breakdown.late is correct here, unlike in some other Gnar matchups: All Out explicitly grants increased healing.
